name: .env Editor
description: Edit dotenv files as a table while keeping comments, order and quoting; export .env.example
help: Parsing and saving run locally in Rust; files never leave your computer.
Comments, blank lines and unrecognizable lines are preserved as-is; variable order never changes and keys, values and inline comments are editable.
Values are shown escaped (\n, \", \\) following the rules used by most dotenv loaders.
The leading switch toggles the export prefix; saving rejects duplicate or invalid keys.
Exporting generates a matching .example file (.env → .env.example) with values cleared and comments kept.

The Compare tab takes 2–8 .env files; the first (starred) is the baseline. Keys in the baseline but not in a file are missing, the reverse are extra; an empty string value is empty; a key repeated in one file is duplicate (its last value is compared); different values are marked as differing. No values are ever shown.

Merging inserts the baseline keys a target lacks right after the preceding baseline key, together with the comments directly above them, keeping export, quoting and inline comments. Values stay empty unless you copy them. You preview before writing, and existing target lines are never changed.
Values are compared literally; $VAR or $(command) are never shell-expanded.
